samasa.vigraha: पुण्या कीर्तिः यस्याः सा पुण्यकीर्तिः
samasa.vigraha_iast: puṇyā kīrtiḥ yasyāḥ sā puṇyakīrtiḥ
samasa.explanation: Inner layer: puṇyā kīrtiḥ 'holy fame' (karmadhāraya: the adjective puṇya qualifies kīrti). Outer layer: a bahuvrīhi, 'She whose fame is holy'. The feminine adjective puṇyā returns to its masculine stem puṇya- in the compound (puṃvadbhāva); kīrti, already feminine, is unchanged. The members meet without sound change.

names.meaning: She whose fame is holy
names.significance: Her renown itself purifies: traditionally, to speak of Her glory is already an act of merit, which the next two names develop.

meaning_check.note: 'or righteous' dropped: puṇya here is 'holy, merit-giving'; the doubled gloss added nothing.

samasa.vigraha: पुण्येन लभ्या पुण्यलभ्या
samasa.vigraha_iast: puṇyena labhyā puṇyalabhyā
samasa.explanation: puṇya 'merit' stands in the instrumental to the gerundive labhyā 'to be attained': 'attainable by (means of) merit'. labhyā is the head.

components.meaning: merit, the fruit of good deeds

components.note: √labh 'to obtain' with the gerundive suffix -ya (yat), feminine

names.meaning: She who is attained through merit
names.significance: Traditionally, devotion to Her and initiation into Her worship are said to come only as the ripened fruit of merit gathered over many lives.

meaning_check.note: puṇya is the instrument, merit itself ('by merit'), not 'righteous souls'; 'only' is the traditional sense rather than a word of the name.

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over an inner itaretara-dvandva and karmadhāraya)
samasa.vigraha: श्रवणम् च कीर्तनम् च श्रवणकीर्तने; पुण्ये श्रवणकीर्तने यस्याः सा पुण्यश्रवणकीर्तना
samasa.vigraha_iast: śravaṇam ca kīrtanam ca śravaṇakīrtane; puṇye śravaṇakīrtane yasyāḥ sā puṇyaśravaṇakīrtanā
samasa.explanation: (1) śravaṇa 'hearing' and kīrtana 'singing, praising' form a dvandva, 'hearing and praising'. (2) puṇya qualifies the pair: 'meritorious hearing and praising' (karmadhāraya). (3) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She, the hearing (of whom) and the praising (of whom) are meritorious'; the neuter kīrtana takes the feminine -ā. She is the object of the hearing and singing, not their agent.

components.note: kīrtana (√kīrt 'to celebrate'), with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She whom it is meritorious to hear of and to praise
names.significance: Śravaṇa and kīrtana head the traditional list of the forms of devotion; simply listening to Her names and singing them is said to yield merit.

meaning_check.note: The previous wording made Her the giver; grammatically the bahuvrīhi says that hearing of Her and praising Her are themselves meritorious. The sense is kept.

names.previous_split_issues: kīrtanā is a noun 'praising' carrying the bahuvrīhi's feminine ending, not 'praising/chanting' as an adjective of Hers.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: पुलोम्नः जाता पुलोमजा; पुलोमजया अर्चिता पुलोमजार्चिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: pulomnaḥ jātā pulomajā; pulomajayā arcitā pulomajārcitā
samasa.explanation: (1) pulomajā 'she who was born of Puloman', i.e. Śacī: the stem puloman (final n dropped in composition) with -ja 'born' from √jan (upapada-tatpuruṣa, feminine -ā). (2) Pulomajā stands in the instrumental to the participle arcitā 'worshipped', which is the head: 'worshipped by Śacī'.

components.meaning: Pulomajā, 'daughter of Puloman': Śacī (Indrāṇī), wife of Indra

names.meaning: She who is worshipped by Pulomajā (Śacī, the wife of Indra)
names.significance: Even Śacī, queen of the gods, worships Her; traditionally her worship is said to keep Indra's sovereignty secure.

meaning_check.note: Capitalization and identification tidied (Pulomajā = Śacī).

names.uncertain: That Śacī's worship secures Indra's rule is a traditional reading; no single source for it was confirmed here.

samasa.vigraha: बन्धस्य मोचनी बन्धमोचनी
samasa.vigraha_iast: bandhasya mocanī bandhamocanī
samasa.explanation: mocanī is an agent noun, 'one who releases'; bandha 'bondage' is its object, expressed in the genitive that goes with an agent noun (kṛd-yoga ṣaṣṭhī). mocanī is the head: 'the releaser from bondage'.

components.note: causative of √muc 'to free', agent noun in -ana, feminine -ī

names.meaning: She who releases from bondage
names.significance: The bondage is outward (prison, debt, trouble) and inward: the bonds of karma and ignorance that tie the self to saṃsāra, from which She alone frees.

meaning_check.note: The first gloss 'She who is free from bonds' does not follow from mocanī, an agent noun ('releaser'); the second gloss is kept.

names.previous_split_issues: bandha was glossed 'band/girdle'; here it is bondage, fetters.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: बन्धुराः अलकाः बन्धुरालकाः; बन्धुराः अलकाः यस्याः सा बन्धुरालका
samasa.vigraha_iast: bandhurāḥ alakāḥ bandhurālakāḥ; bandhurāḥ alakāḥ yasyāḥ sā bandhurālakā
samasa.explanation: Inner layer: bandhura 'wavy' qualifies alaka 'lock of hair, curl' (karmadhāraya). Outer layer: a bahuvrīhi, 'She whose locks are wavy'; alaka takes the feminine -ā.

components.meaning: locks of hair, curls (especially on the forehead)
components.note: alaka, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She whose locks of hair are wavy
names.significance: A return to the description of Her beauty: the gently curling locks framing Her face.

meaning_check.note: Stray semicolon removed and wording aligned with the bahuvrīhi.

names.uncertain: The reading itself: this edition follows the verse text (bandhurālakā) where the old name list read barbarālakā; which of the two Bhāskararāya's text adopts could not be confirmed here. The sense is the same either way.
names.variants: The source's name list reads बर्बरालका barbarālakā (barbara 'curly'); the verse text, followed here, reads बन्धुरालका. Both readings are current in printed editions.

samasa.vigraha: विमर्शः एव रूपम् विमर्शरूपम्; विमर्शरूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति विमर्शरूपिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: vimarśaḥ eva rūpam vimarśarūpam; vimarśarūpam asyāḥ asti iti vimarśarūpiṇī
samasa.explanation: vimarśa-rūpa 'the form that is vimarśa' is a karmadhāraya of identification. The possessive suffix -in (Pāṇini 5.2.115 ata iniṭhanau) and the feminine -ī make rūpiṇī 'having the form of': 'She whose form is vimarśa'.

components.meaning: vimarśa: reflective self-awareness, consciousness turned upon itself

names.meaning: She whose form is vimarśa, the reflective awareness of consciousness
names.significance: In Śrīvidyā and Kashmir Śaivism, Śiva is prakāśa, the light of consciousness, and Śakti is vimarśa, its power to know itself; without vimarśa the light would be inert. The Goddess is that self-knowing power.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'vimarsha' put into IAST; 'reflection or meaning' replaced by the technical sense, reflective self-awareness.

components.meaning: knowledge, wisdom; also a mantra (especially a mantra of a goddess)

names.meaning: She who is in the form of knowledge
names.significance: She is the liberating knowledge that dispels ignorance (avidyā); in Śrīvidyā, vidyā also means the mantra, so She is the mantra as well as the knowledge it gives.

sandhi.rule: jaśtva: a final t becomes d at the end of a member, here before a vowel (Pāṇini 8.2.39 jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte)

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner bahuvrīhi and karmadhāraya)
samasa.vigraha: वियत् आदिः यस्य तत् वियदादि; वियदादि जगत् वियदादिजगत्; वियदादिजगतः प्रसूः वियदादिजगत्प्रसूः
samasa.vigraha_iast: viyat ādiḥ yasya tat viyadādi; viyadādi jagat viyadādijagat; viyadādijagataḥ prasūḥ viyadādijagatprasūḥ
samasa.explanation: (1) viyad-ādi 'that which begins with ether (space)': a bahuvrīhi in -ādi, 'having viyat as its first'. (2) It qualifies jagat 'the world' (karmadhāraya): 'the world beginning with ether', i.e. the whole order of the elements from space down to earth. (3) prasū 'mother, she who brings forth' is the head; the world stands to it in the genitive. At jagat-prasū the t stays unvoiced before p.

components.note: present participle of √gam, used as a noun
pra + √sū 'to give birth', root noun; ū-stem, nominative -ūḥ

names.meaning: She who is the mother of the world, which begins with ether
names.significance: The world unfolds from Her as the five elements, ether first, as in the Taittirīya Upaniṣad (2.1): from the Self, space; from space, air; and so on down to earth.

meaning_check.note: Shortened to follow the compound: the world that begins with ether (viyat), not 'the aggregate of all the elements'.

names.previous_split_issues: viyadādi jagat was given as one row in its sandhi form; it is viyat 'ether' + ādi 'beginning with' + jagat 'world'. The name was printed as two words; it is one compound (corrected).

samasa.vigraha: सर्वे व्याधयः सर्वव्याधयः; सर्वव्याधीनाम् प्रशमनी सर्वव्याधिप्रशमनी
samasa.vigraha_iast: sarve vyādhayaḥ sarvavyādhayaḥ; sarvavyādhīnām praśamanī sarvavyādhipraśamanī
samasa.explanation: (1) sarva-vyādhi 'all diseases' (karmadhāraya: sarva qualifies vyādhi). (2) praśamanī 'she who allays' is an agent noun and the head; the diseases are its object in the genitive.

components.note: pra + causative of √śam 'to be calm', agent noun in -ana, feminine -ī

names.meaning: She who allays all diseases
names.significance: Traditionally both the illnesses of the body and the root disease of saṃsāra (bhava-roga) are meant; recitation of this name is customary for healing.

meaning_check.note: 'and sorrows' is not in the name; the sense of all diseases is kept.

samasa.vigraha: सर्वे मृत्यवः सर्वमृत्यवः; सर्वमृत्यूनाम् निवारिणी सर्वमृत्युनिवारिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: sarve mṛtyavaḥ sarvamṛtyavaḥ; sarvamṛtyūnām nivāriṇī sarvamṛtyunivāriṇī
samasa.explanation: (1) sarva-mṛtyu 'every death', i.e. death in all its forms (karmadhāraya). (2) nivāriṇī 'she who wards off' is the head and takes the deaths as its object in the genitive.

components.note: ni + causative of √vṛ 'to cover, restrain', agent suffix -in, feminine -ī; n becomes ṇ after r (ṇatva)

names.meaning: She who wards off every kind of death
names.significance: Traditionally untimely death (apamṛtyu) is meant, and beyond it the endless round of dying and being born, which ends in knowledge of Her.

meaning_check.note: The previous text was truncated ('guards Her devotees from all') and omitted death (mṛtyu), the object of the name.

samasa.vigraha: अग्रे गण्या अग्रगण्या
samasa.vigraha_iast: agre gaṇyā agragaṇyā
samasa.explanation: agra 'the front, the first place' stands in the locative to the gerundive gaṇyā 'to be counted': 'to be counted in the first place', foremost. gaṇyā is the head.

names.meaning: She who is to be counted the foremost
names.significance: Whenever beings are reckoned up, She is counted first: She precedes the gods themselves.

meaning_check.note: Wording brought closer to gaṇyā 'to be counted' (previously 'considered').

samasa.vigraha: न चिन्त्यम् अचिन्त्यम्; अचिन्त्यम् रूपम् यस्याः सा अचिन्त्यरूपा
samasa.vigraha_iast: na cintyam acintyam; acintyam rūpam yasyāḥ sā acintyarūpā
samasa.explanation: (1) a-cintya 'not to be thought, inconceivable': a nañ-tatpuruṣa, the negative na appearing as a- before a consonant (a morphological replacement, Pāṇini 6.3.73 nalopo nañaḥ, not sound-sandhi). (2) A bahuvrīhi: 'She whose form is inconceivable'; rūpa takes the feminine -ā.

components.note: rūpa, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She whose form is beyond the reach of thought
names.significance: Her true form cannot be made an object of the mind, which itself arises in Her; the Kena Upaniṣad says of Brahman that it is not what the mind thinks but that by which the mind thinks.

meaning_check.note: 'is of a form' simplified to the bahuvrīhi 'whose form'; sense unchanged.

samasa.vigraha: कलेः कल्मषाणि कलिकल्मषाणि; कलिकल्मषाणाम् नाशिनी कलिकल्मषनाशिनी
samasa.vigraha_iast: kaleḥ kalmaṣāṇi kalikalmaṣāṇi; kalikalmaṣāṇām nāśinī kalikalmaṣanāśinī
samasa.explanation: (1) kali-kalmaṣa 'the impurities of the Kali age' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) nāśinī 'she who destroys' is the head and takes them as object in the genitive.

components.meaning: the Kali age, the last and darkest of the four ages; also strife

components.note: causative of √naś 'to perish', agent suffix -in, feminine -ī

names.meaning: She who destroys the sins of the Kali age
names.significance: The faults peculiar to the Kali age (impurity, forgetfulness of dharma, strife) are cleansed by the remembrance of Her names, traditionally the chief means for this age.

meaning_check.note: Capitalization (Kali).

components.note: patronymic chain: Kata (a sage) → Kātya 'descendant of Kata' → Kātyāyana 'descendant of Kātya' → Kātyāyanī, the female of that line

names.meaning: She who is Kātyāyanī, daughter of the sage Kātyāyana of Kata's line
names.significance: In the Purāṇas the Goddess born from the united radiance of the gods to slay Mahiṣa was first worshipped by, or born in the hermitage of, the sage Kātyāyana, and so is called Kātyāyanī; She is the Durgā of the Devī-Māhātmya.

meaning_check.note: The patronymic names Kātyāyana, a descendant of the sage Kata, not Kata himself; capitalization tidied.

names.uncertain: Purāṇic accounts differ on whether She was born in Kātyāyana's hermitage or first worshipped by him; the derivation from Kata is standard grammar.

samasa.vigraha: कालस्य हन्त्री कालहन्त्री
samasa.vigraha_iast: kālasya hantrī kālahantrī
samasa.explanation: hantrī 'slayer' is an agent noun (hantṛ, feminine -ī) and the head; kāla is its object in the genitive.

components.meaning: time; also death, Yama, who comes with time

components.note: hantṛ (√han 'to strike, slay' + agent suffix -tṛ), feminine -ī

names.meaning: She who is the destroyer of time (death)
names.significance: For Her devotee She ends death; at the great dissolution She withdraws time itself, which devours all else.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: कमले इव अक्षिणी यस्य सः कमलाक्षः; कमलाक्षेण निषेविता कमलाक्षनिषेविता
samasa.vigraha_iast: kamale iva akṣiṇī yasya saḥ kamalākṣaḥ; kamalākṣeṇa niṣevitā kamalākṣaniṣevitā
samasa.explanation: (1) kamalākṣa 'he whose eyes are like lotuses', Viṣṇu: a bahuvrīhi in which akṣi 'eye' becomes akṣa (the compound-final suffix ṣac, Pāṇini 5.4.113 bahuvrīhau sakthyakṣṇoḥ svāṅgāt ṣac). (2) He stands in the instrumental to the participle niṣevitā 'served, resorted to', which is the head.

components.note: ni + √sev 'to serve, attend', past participle, feminine

names.meaning: She who is served and worshipped by lotus-eyed Viṣṇu
names.significance: Viṣṇu Himself attends on Her; traditionally He is counted among Her worshippers, and the power by which He preserves the world is Hers.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'viShNu' put into IAST; niṣevitā 'served, resorted to' rendered more fully than 'takes refuge'.

samasa.vigraha: ताम्बूलेन पूरितम् ताम्बूलपूरितम्; ताम्बूलपूरितम् मुखम् यस्याः सा ताम्बूलपूरितमुखी
samasa.vigraha_iast: tāmbūlena pūritam tāmbūlapūritam; tāmbūlapūritam mukham yasyāḥ sā tāmbūlapūritamukhī
samasa.explanation: (1) tāmbūla-pūrita 'filled with betel' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa: tāmbūla is the instrument of the participle pūrita). (2) A bahuvrīhi with mukha 'mouth': 'She whose mouth is filled with betel'. A bahuvrīhi ending in a body-part word takes the feminine -ī (Pāṇini 4.1.54 svāṅgāc copasarjanād asaṃyogopadhāt), hence mukhī.

components.meaning: betel (the rolled betel leaf with areca and spices)

components.note: mukha, with the feminine -ī of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She whose mouth is filled with betel
names.significance: The red betel deepens the crimson of Her lips (name 24), and its camphor fragrance is the theme of name 26; in Her worship tāmbūla is offered among the closing courtly attentions.

meaning_check.note: 'from chewing' is not in the name; the compound says the mouth is filled with betel.

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi of resemblance (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: दाडिम्याः कुसुमम् दाडिमीकुसुमम्; दाडिमीकुसुमस्य प्रभा इव प्रभा यस्याः सा दाडिमीकुसुमप्रभा
samasa.vigraha_iast: dāḍimyāḥ kusumam dāḍimīkusumam; dāḍimīkusumasya prabhā iva prabhā yasyāḥ sā dāḍimīkusumaprabhā
samasa.explanation: (1) dāḍimī-kusuma 'the pomegranate flower' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) A bahuvrīhi of resemblance: 'She whose radiance is (like) the radiance of the pomegranate flower'. prabhā is already feminine.

names.meaning: She who shines like a pomegranate flower
names.significance: The pomegranate blossom is a deep scarlet: Her complexion is the rosy red (aruṇa) of the meditation verses, the color of compassion.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: मृगस्य अक्षिणी इव अक्षिणी यस्याः सा मृगाक्षी
samasa.vigraha_iast: mṛgasya akṣiṇī iva akṣiṇī yasyāḥ sā mṛgākṣī
samasa.explanation: A bahuvrīhi of comparison: 'She whose eyes are like a deer's'. akṣi 'eye' becomes -akṣa at the end of the bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 5.4.113) and then takes the feminine -ī: mṛgākṣī.

components.note: akṣi 'eye' → -akṣa, with the feminine -ī of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She whose eyes are long and beautiful like those of a doe
names.significance: The doe's eye is the classical image of eyes that are large, long and gently restless.

components.note: causative of √muh 'to be bewildered', agent suffix -in, feminine -ī

names.meaning: She who is enchanting
names.significance: She enchants all by Her beauty and, as Mahāmāyā, casts the spell by which the world forgets itself. Traditionally the Mohinī form Viṣṇu took at the churning of the ocean is regarded as Hers.

components.note: mukha 'mouth, front' + the suffix -ya: 'being at the head'

names.meaning: She who is the first
names.significance: She stands at the head of all: the first of the gods and the source from which they come.

components.note: mṛḍa 'the Gracious', a name of Śiva, + the augment ān and feminine -ī (Pāṇini 4.1.49 indravaruṇabhavaśarvarudramṛḍa…), as in bhavānī, rudrāṇī

names.meaning: She who is the wife of Mṛḍa (Śiva)
names.significance: Mṛḍa means 'the gracious one', from √mṛḍ 'to be kind': as His consort She is the grace by which Śiva blesses.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'mRiDa (shiva)' put into IAST.

samasa.vigraha: मित्रम् एव रूपम् मित्ररूपम्; मित्ररूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति मित्ररूपिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: mitram eva rūpam mitrarūpam; mitrarūpam asyāḥ asti iti mitrarūpiṇī
samasa.explanation: mitra-rūpa 'the form of a friend' (karmadhāraya of identification), with the possessive -in and feminine -ī: 'She who has the form of a friend'. mitra (neuter) is 'friend'; the masculine Mitra is the sun-god, one of the Ādityas, and the name allows that reading too.

components.meaning: friend; as a proper name, Mitra, the sun-god

names.meaning: She who has the form of a friend (to all beings)
names.significance: She is the friend of the whole world, wishing good to all without being asked; traditionally the name is also read as Her being the sun (Mitra), one of the twelve Ādityas.

meaning_check.note: '(universe)' replaced by the plain sense; the reading as the sun-god Mitra is added in the significance.

samasa.vigraha: नित्यम् तृप्ता नित्यतृप्ता
samasa.vigraha_iast: nityam tṛptā nityatṛptā
samasa.explanation: nitya 'always' qualifies the participle tṛptā 'contented', which is the head: 'ever contented'.

names.meaning: She who is eternally contented
names.significance: Lacking nothing, She needs nothing; She accepts offerings for the devotee's sake, not Her own.

samasa.vigraha: भक्तानाम् निधिः भक्तनिधिः
samasa.vigraha_iast: bhaktānām nidhiḥ bhaktanidhiḥ
samasa.explanation: nidhi 'treasure' is the head and the devotees stand to it in the genitive: 'the treasure of the devotees'. nidhi is masculine and keeps its form in a name of the Goddess (in apposition).

components.note: ni + √dhā 'to place'; masculine i-stem, nominative singular

names.meaning: She who is the treasure of the devotees
names.significance: To Her devotees She is the inexhaustible store from which every good, worldly and spiritual, is drawn.

components.meaning: controller, ruler, she who restrains and governs
components.note: ni + √yam 'to restrain' + the agent suffix -tṛ, feminine -ī

names.meaning: She who controls and governs all beings
names.significance: As the inner controller (antaryāmin) She directs every being from within and keeps it on its course.

meaning_check.note: 'guides on the right path' is interpretation; niyantrī is the one who restrains and governs (ni + √yam). The guiding sense is kept in the significance.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: निखिलस्य ईश्वरी निखिलेश्वरी
samasa.vigraha_iast: nikhilasya īśvarī nikhileśvarī
samasa.explanation: īśvarī 'sovereign' is the head and nikhila 'all, the whole' stands to it in the genitive: 'the ruler of all'.

names.meaning: She who is the ruler of all
names.significance: Nothing lies outside Her rule: She is sovereign over the whole, without remainder.

sandhi.rule: yaṇ: ī becomes y before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci)

samasa.type: tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner bahuvrīhi and karmadhāraya)
samasa.vigraha: मैत्री आदिः यासाम् ताः मैत्र्यादयः; मैत्र्यादयः वासनाः मैत्र्यादिवासनाः; मैत्र्यादिवासनाभिः लभ्या मैत्र्यादिवासनालभ्या
samasa.vigraha_iast: maitrī ādiḥ yāsām tāḥ maitryādayaḥ; maitryādayaḥ vāsanāḥ maitryādivāsanāḥ; maitryādivāsanābhiḥ labhyā maitryādivāsanālabhyā
samasa.explanation: (1) maitry-ādi 'those beginning with friendliness' (bahuvrīhi in -ādi). (2) These qualify vāsanā 'dispositions, cultivated attitudes' (karmadhāraya). (3) The gerundive labhyā 'attainable' is the head; the dispositions are its instrument: 'attainable through friendliness and the other dispositions'.

names.meaning: She who is attained through friendliness and the other good dispositions
names.significance: The four are those of Yoga Sūtra 1.33: friendliness toward the happy, compassion toward the suffering, gladness toward the virtuous and equanimity toward the wicked, by which the mind becomes clear; a mind so cleared finds Her.

meaning_check.note: maitrī is friendliness, goodwill, not 'love'; the reference to the four attitudes is given in the significance.

samasa.vigraha: महान् प्रलयः महाप्रलयः; महाप्रलयस्य साक्षिणी महाप्रलयसाक्षिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: mahān pralayaḥ mahāpralayaḥ; mahāpralayasya sākṣiṇī mahāpralayasākṣiṇī
samasa.explanation: (1) mahā-pralaya 'the great dissolution' (karmadhāraya; mahat becomes mahā- before a co-referential member, Pāṇini 6.3.46). (2) sākṣiṇī 'witness' is the head and takes the dissolution in the genitive.

names.meaning: She who is witness to the great dissolution
names.significance: When all the worlds and even the gods are dissolved, She alone remains, watching; compare name 232, where She witnesses Śiva's great dance at the end of the aeon.

components.note: feminine of para, agreeing with śaktiḥ. Not a compound but a phrase of two words: the adjective parā agrees with the noun, and the pair is counted as one name. Had they been compounded as a karmadhāraya, the feminine parā would normally return to the masculine stem (puṃvadbhāva, Pāṇini 6.3.42): para-. The verse text accordingly prints them as two words.
√śak 'to be able'; feminine i-stem, nominative singular

names.meaning: She who is the supreme Power (Parā Śakti)
names.significance: The one power inseparable from Śiva, from which the powers of will, knowledge and action (name 658) and every lesser power proceed.

meaning_check.note: 'original' is not in the name; parā is 'supreme'. The title Parā Śakti is given in IAST.

names.uncertain: Phrase or compound: the retained feminine parā and the verse's spacing point to two words in agreement (no samāsa); in later usage Parāśakti is also treated as a fixed compound title.

sandhi.rule: after a prefix ending in i, the s of sthā becomes ṣ (Pāṇini 8.3.65), and th then becomes ṭh by retroflex assimilation (8.4.41 ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ), inside the word niṣṭhā

components.note: feminine of para, agreeing with niṣṭhā; as in name 572 the two words stand in agreement and are not compounded (a karmadhāraya would normally give para-).

components.meaning: culmination, final goal; firm ground, steadfast abiding

names.meaning: She who is the supreme end, the supreme abidance
names.significance: She is the culmination in which every path comes to rest: the Gītā (3.3) speaks of two kinds of niṣṭhā, of knowledge and of action, and both end in Her.
names.uncertain: Phrase or compound, as with name 572: the feminine parā is kept, so the name is read as two words in agreement.

samasa.type: karmadhāraya (identification) with the possessive suffix -in (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: प्रज्ञानस्य घनः प्रज्ञानघनः; प्रज्ञानघनः एव रूपम् प्रज्ञानघनरूपम्; प्रज्ञानघनरूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति प्रज्ञानघनरूपिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: prajñānasya ghanaḥ prajñānaghanaḥ; prajñānaghanaḥ eva rūpam prajñānaghanarūpam; prajñānaghanarūpam asyāḥ asti iti prajñānaghanarūpiṇī
samasa.explanation: (1) prajñāna-ghana 'a solid mass of consciousness' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, like saindhava-ghana 'a lump of salt'). (2) It is identified with rūpa 'form' (karmadhāraya). (3) The possessive -in and feminine -ī: 'She whose form is a solid mass of consciousness'.

components.note: √han; at the end of a compound 'consisting wholly of'

names.meaning: She whose form is a solid mass of pure consciousness
names.significance: The phrase is Upaniṣadic: the Bṛhadāraṇyaka (4.5.13) says that as a lump of salt is salt throughout, so the Self is prajñānaghana, consciousness through and through, with no inside or outside; the Māṇḍūkya (5) uses the same word.

meaning_check.note: 'pure, condensed knowledge' rendered as the Upaniṣadic 'solid mass of consciousness'; rūpiṇī 'whose form is' made explicit.

names.previous_split_issues: rūpiṇī was misspelt rupiṇī (short u); corrected.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: माध्व्याः पानम् माध्वीपानम्; माध्वीपानेन अलसा माध्वीपानालसा
samasa.vigraha_iast: mādhvyāḥ pānam mādhvīpānam; mādhvīpānena alasā mādhvīpānālasā
samasa.explanation: (1) mādhvī-pāna 'the drinking of honey-wine' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) alasā 'languid' is the head and the drinking is its cause, in the instrumental: 'languid from drinking honey-wine'.

components.meaning: mādhvī, a sweet wine made from honey or madhūka flowers

names.meaning: She who is languid from drinking honey-wine
names.significance: Traditionally read inwardly: the wine is the bliss of the Self, and Her languor is the absence of all striving, since for Her nothing remains to be gained.

meaning_check.note: The second gloss 'She who is not eager for anything' is the traditional inner reading, not the meaning of the words; it is moved to the significance.

names.previous_split_issues: pānālasā was left as one row; it is pāna 'drinking' + alasā 'languid', joined by savarṇa-dīrgha.

components.note: √mad 'to rejoice, be intoxicated', past participle, feminine

names.meaning: She who is intoxicated
names.significance: Traditionally, the intoxication is the bliss of Her own Self, which needs nothing outside it.

samasa.type: karmadhāraya (identification) with the possessive suffix -in (over an inner karmadhāraya)
samasa.vigraha: मातृकाः एव वर्णाः मातृकावर्णाः; मातृकावर्णाः एव रूपम् मातृकावर्णरूपम्; मातृकावर्णरूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति मातृकावर्णरूपिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: mātṛkāḥ eva varṇāḥ mātṛkāvarṇāḥ; mātṛkāvarṇāḥ eva rūpam mātṛkāvarṇarūpam; mātṛkāvarṇarūpam asyāḥ asti iti mātṛkāvarṇarūpiṇī
samasa.explanation: (1) mātṛkā-varṇa 'the letters that are the mātṛkā' (karmadhāraya; a genitive reading, 'the letters of the mātṛkā', comes to the same). (2) Identified with rūpa 'form'. (3) The possessive -in and feminine -ī: 'She whose form is the letters of the mātṛkā'.

components.meaning: mātṛkā, the 'little mothers': the letters of the Sanskrit alphabet as the matrix of all speech and mantra

names.meaning: She who is in the form of the letters of the alphabet
names.significance: The mātṛkā are the fifty letters from a to kṣa; in mātṛkā-nyāsa they are placed on the worshipper's body as on Hers, since every mantra and every word is made of them.

samasa.vigraha: महान् कैलासः महाकैलासः; महाकैलासः निलयः यस्याः सा महाकैलासनिलया
samasa.vigraha_iast: mahān kailāsaḥ mahākailāsaḥ; mahākailāsaḥ nilayaḥ yasyāḥ sā mahākailāsanilayā
samasa.explanation: (1) mahā-kailāsa 'the great Kailāsa' (karmadhāraya; mahat becomes mahā-, Pāṇini 6.3.46). (2) A bahuvrīhi with nilaya 'dwelling': 'She whose dwelling is the great Kailāsa'; nilaya takes the feminine -ā.

components.meaning: Kailāsa, the mountain abode of Śiva

components.note: nilaya (ni + √lī 'to settle'), with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who dwells in the great Kailāsa
names.significance: Mahākailāsa is traditionally the supreme abode of Śiva and Śakti, beyond the earthly mountain; inwardly it is placed at the crown of the head.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'kailAsa' put into IAST; wording tidied.

sandhi.rule: final s becomes r (ru) before a voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ); the r stays before l

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over an upamita-karmadhāraya and an upamāna-karmadhāraya)
samasa.vigraha: दोः लता इव दोर्लता; मृणालम् इव मृदु मृणालमृदु; मृणालमृद्वी दोर्लता यस्याः सा मृणालमृदुदोर्लता
samasa.vigraha_iast: doḥ latā iva dorlatā; mṛṇālam iva mṛdu mṛṇālamṛdu; mṛṇālamṛdvī dorlatā yasyāḥ sā mṛṇālamṛdudorlatā
samasa.explanation: (1) dor-latā 'an arm (slender) as a creeper': the thing compared comes first and the standard second (upamita-karmadhāraya, Pāṇini 2.1.56). (2) mṛṇāla-mṛdu 'soft as a lotus stalk': standard of comparison + shared quality (upamāna-karmadhāraya, Pāṇini 2.1.55). (3) A bahuvrīhi: 'She whose creeper-like arms are soft as lotus stalks'. The feminine mṛdvī appears as the stem mṛdu (puṃvadbhāva); latā is already feminine. The singular stands for the class: She has four arms (name 7).

components.meaning: lotus stalk, the fibrous lotus root

components.note: s-stem; dos becomes dor- before l

names.meaning: She whose creeper-like arms are as soft as lotus stalks
names.significance: Her four arms are slender and graceful like creepers and tender like the lotus stalk, a stock image of classical poetry.

meaning_check.note: 'and cool' is not in the name; latā 'creeper' was not rendered.

names.previous_split_issues: dorlatā was left as one row; it is dos 'arm' + latā 'creeper' (s → r before l).

components.meaning: worthy of worship, to be honored, glorious
components.note: √mah 'to honor, magnify' + the gerundive suffix -anīya, feminine

names.meaning: She who is worthy of adoration
names.significance: Being greatest, She alone is wholly worthy of worship; traditionally all honor offered anywhere is said to reach Her in the end.

meaning_check.note: 'adorable' carries a different sense in modern English; mahanīyā is 'to be worshipped, worthy of honor'.

samasa.vigraha: दयायाः मूर्तिः दयामूर्तिः; अथवा दया मूर्तिः यस्याः सा दयामूर्तिः
samasa.vigraha_iast: dayāyāḥ mūrtiḥ dayāmūrtiḥ; athavā dayā mūrtiḥ yasyāḥ sā dayāmūrtiḥ
samasa.explanation: As a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, mūrti 'embodiment' is the head: 'the embodiment of compassion'. As a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose form is compassion'. mūrti is feminine, so the form is the same either way.

components.note: √murch 'to take shape'; feminine i-stem, nominative singular

names.meaning: She who is the personification of compassion
names.significance: She took form at all only out of compassion, appearing from the fire for the gods' sake (names 4–5); compassion is Her very body.

samasa.vigraha: महत् साम्राज्यम् महासाम्राज्यम्; महासाम्राज्येन शालिनी महासाम्राज्यशालिनी
samasa.vigraha_iast: mahat sāmrājyam mahāsāmrājyam; mahāsāmrājyena śālinī mahāsāmrājyaśālinī
samasa.explanation: (1) mahā-sāmrājya 'great sovereignty, the great empire' (karmadhāraya; mahat → mahā-, Pāṇini 6.3.46). (2) śālinī 'possessed of, resplendent with' is the head and takes the empire in the instrumental.

components.note: from samrāj 'universal ruler'; in sam + rāj the m stays m, not anusvāra (Pāṇini 8.3.25 mo rāji samaḥ kvau)

components.meaning: possessed of, abounding in, resplendent with

names.meaning: She who possesses the great empire, sovereign over all
names.significance: Her empire is the whole of creation: the worlds, their gods and their guardians are within Her rule.

meaning_check.note: 'of the three worlds' is not in the name; the scope of Her sovereignty is given in the significance.

samasa.vigraha: आत्मनः विद्या आत्मविद्या
samasa.vigraha_iast: ātmanaḥ vidyā ātmavidyā
samasa.explanation: vidyā 'knowledge' is the head and ātman 'the Self' stands to it in the genitive: 'knowledge of the Self'. ātman drops its final n in composition.

components.note: appears as ātma- (final n dropped in composition, Pāṇini 8.2.7)

names.meaning: She who is the knowledge of the Self
names.significance: She is the knowledge of the Self taught in the Upaniṣads, which the Gītā (10.32) calls the foremost of all knowledges.

samasa.vigraha: महती विद्या महाविद्या
samasa.vigraha_iast: mahatī vidyā mahāvidyā
samasa.explanation: mahatī 'great' qualifies vidyā; the feminine adjective takes the masculine stem (puṃvadbhāva, Pāṇini 6.3.42) and mahat becomes mahā- (6.3.46), as in name 2.

names.meaning: She who is the great knowledge
names.significance: In the Tantras mahāvidyā is the great mantra-knowledge, and the name is given to the ten Wisdom Goddesses (daśa mahāvidyā), all regarded as Her forms.

meaning_check.note: 'the seat of' is not in the name, and 'the knowledge of the self' belongs to name 583.

samasa.vigraha: श्रीः विद्या श्रीविद्या; अथवा श्रियः विद्या श्रीविद्या
samasa.vigraha_iast: śrīḥ vidyā śrīvidyā; athavā śriyaḥ vidyā śrīvidyā
samasa.explanation: As a karmadhāraya, śrī qualifies vidyā: 'the auspicious knowledge'. As a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa: 'the knowledge (mantra) of Śrī', the Goddess. vidyā is the head either way.

names.meaning: She who is Śrīvidyā, the auspicious knowledge (the Pañcadaśī mantra)
names.significance: Śrīvidyā names both Her fifteen-syllable mantra, the Pañcadaśī, and the whole tradition of Her worship; the mantra is Her subtle body (names 85–89).

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'pa~nchadashi' put into IAST; the title Śrīvidyā given.

samasa.vigraha: कामेन सेविता कामसेविता
samasa.vigraha_iast: kāmena sevitā kāmasevitā
samasa.explanation: Kāma stands in the instrumental to the participle sevitā 'worshipped', which is the head: 'worshipped by Kāma'.

names.meaning: She who is worshipped by Kāmadeva
names.significance: Kāma, revived by Her after Śiva's eye burned him (name 84), is traditionally counted among the twelve great worshippers of Śrīvidyā, and the kādi form of the Pañcadaśī is called the Kāmarāja-vidyā after him. Compare name 375, kāmapūjitā.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'kAmadeva' put into IAST.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: षोडशानाम् अक्षराणाम् समाहारः षोडशाक्षरी; षोडशाक्षरी विद्या षोडशाक्षरीविद्या; श्रीः षोडशाक्षरीविद्या श्रीषोडशाक्षरीविद्या
samasa.vigraha_iast: ṣoḍaśānām akṣarāṇām samāhāraḥ ṣoḍaśākṣarī; ṣoḍaśākṣarī vidyā ṣoḍaśākṣarīvidyā; śrīḥ ṣoḍaśākṣarīvidyā śrīṣoḍaśākṣarīvidyā
samasa.explanation: (1) ṣoḍaśākṣarī 'the group of sixteen syllables': a collective numeral compound (samāhāra-dvigu); a dvigu ending in -a takes the feminine -ī (Pāṇini 4.1.21 dvigoḥ). (2) It stands in apposition to vidyā 'mantra' (karmadhāraya): 'the sixteen-syllable mantra'. Being a collective noun, not an adjective, it keeps its -ī. (3) śrī qualifies the whole as in names 1–3.

components.note: ṣaṣ 'six' + daśan 'ten', irregularly ṣoḍaśan (Pāṇini 6.3.109 pṛṣodarādīni yathopadiṣṭam); appears as ṣoḍaśa-
akṣara, with the -ī of the dvigu

names.meaning: She who is the auspicious sixteen-syllable Vidyā (the Ṣoḍaśī mantra)
names.significance: Traditionally the Ṣoḍaśī is the Pañcadaśī completed by a sixteenth seed-syllable (śrīṃ), the highest form of Her mantra, imparted only at the final initiation.

meaning_check.note: 'in the form of' replaced by the identity the karmadhāraya states; Vidyā here is the mantra, and śrī is rendered.

names.uncertain: The composition of the Ṣoḍaśī (which syllable completes the Pañcadaśī, and where it is placed) differs between lineages; the significance gives the commonest account.

samasa.vigraha: त्रयः कूटाः यस्याः सा त्रिकूटा
samasa.vigraha_iast: trayaḥ kūṭāḥ yasyāḥ sā trikūṭā
samasa.explanation: A bahuvrīhi with a numeral first member: 'She who has three kūṭas'. kūṭa takes the feminine -ā.

components.meaning: section, group (of syllables in a mantra); literally peak, summit
components.note: kūṭa, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who has three sections (the three kūṭas of the Pañcadaśī mantra)
names.significance: The Pañcadaśī falls into three kūṭas, vāgbhava, kāmarāja and śakti, which are Her face, Her middle body and the body below the waist (names 85–87); traditionally every triad (the three worlds, guṇas, states, deities) is read in them.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'pa~nchadashI' put into IAST; 'is in the three parts' rendered as the bahuvrīhi 'has three sections'.

names.previous_split_issues: kūṭā was glossed 'peak'; here it is a section of the mantra (peak is the literal sense).

samasa.vigraha: कामः कोटिः यस्याः सा कामकोटिका
samasa.vigraha_iast: kāmaḥ koṭiḥ yasyāḥ sā kāmakoṭikā
samasa.explanation: A bahuvrīhi, 'She of whom Kāma is a koṭi (a portion)', with the optional bahuvrīhi suffix -ka (kap, Pāṇini 5.4.154 śeṣād vibhāṣā) and the feminine -ā. Kāma here is Kāmeśvara, Śiva as Her lover.

components.meaning: a portion, a part; also extremity, highest point

names.meaning: She of whom Kāma (Kāmeśvara, Śiva) is but a part
names.significance: Even Kāmeśvara, Her consort, is a portion of Her: Śiva and Śakti are one, and the whole is Hers.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS put into IAST; 'or an approximate form' dropped as unclear.

names.previous_split_issues: koṭikā was glossed 'crore/ten million'; here koṭi is 'portion' (or 'extremity').
names.uncertain: koṭi has several senses (portion, extremity, ten million), and the name is also read as 'She who dwells at Kāmakoṭi', the pīṭha at Kāñcī. The meaning follows the reading of Kāma as a part of Her.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ), inside the lexicalised compound kaṭākṣa 'side-glance'

samasa.type: tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner cvi-compound, ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas and a karmadhāraya)
samasa.vigraha: अकिङ्कर्यः किङ्कर्यः भूताः किङ्करीभूताः; कटाक्षस्य किङ्करीभूताः कटाक्षकिङ्करीभूताः; कमलानाम् कोटयः कमलाकोटयः; कटाक्षकिङ्करीभूताः कमलाकोटयः कटाक्षकिङ्करीभूतकमलाकोटयः; ताभिः सेविता कटाक्षकिङ्करीभूतकमलाकोटिसेविता
samasa.vigraha_iast: akiṅkaryaḥ kiṅkaryaḥ bhūtāḥ kiṅkarībhūtāḥ; kaṭākṣasya kiṅkarībhūtāḥ kaṭākṣakiṅkarībhūtāḥ; kamalānām koṭayaḥ kamalākoṭayaḥ; kaṭākṣakiṅkarībhūtāḥ kamalākoṭayaḥ kaṭākṣakiṅkarībhūtakamalākoṭayaḥ; tābhiḥ sevitā kaṭākṣakiṅkarībhūtakamalākoṭisevitā
samasa.explanation: (1) kiṅkarī-bhūta 'become handmaids' (those who were not handmaids have become so): the cvi construction with √bhū (Pāṇini 5.4.50), whose -ī also replaces a final a (7.4.32 asya cvau), so the surface is the same whether one starts from kiṅkara or the feminine kiṅkarī. (2) kaṭākṣa-kiṅkarībhūta 'become handmaids of (Her) side-glance' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) kamalā-koṭi 'millions of Lakṣmīs' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa), qualified by (2) (karmadhāraya). (4) The participle sevitā 'served' is the head of the whole and takes them in the instrumental.

components.note: kiṅkara 'servant' (lit. 'what shall I do?'); the -ī is the cvi vowel / feminine

names.meaning: She who is attended by millions of Lakṣmīs who have become handmaids of Her side-glance
names.significance: A single glance from Her brings forth fortune upon fortune: countless Lakṣmīs wait on that glance as servants. Traditionally, a mere glance of Her grace makes the devotee prosperous.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'lakShmis' and the typo 'Hern' corrected; kiṅkarībhūta 'become handmaids (of the glance)' rendered more exactly than 'subdued by Her glances'.

names.uncertain: kaṭākṣa may be taken in the genitive ('handmaids of Her glance') or the instrumental ('made handmaids by Her glance'); the image is the same.

sandhi.rule: final s becomes visarga (Pāṇini 8.2.66 with 8.3.15), and the visarga stays before a sibilant followed by a hard consonant (8.3.35 śarpare visarjanīyaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: शिरसि स्थिता शिरःस्थिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: śirasi sthitā śiraḥsthitā
samasa.explanation: The participle sthitā 'abiding' is the head and śiras 'head' stands to it in the locative: 'abiding in the head'.

components.note: s-stem; śiras becomes śiraḥ before sth

names.meaning: She who resides in the head
names.significance: Names 591–597 place Her at four points of the body for meditation; here, at the crown of the head, She is meditated on as shining like the moon (name 592).

samasa.vigraha: चन्द्रस्य निभा इव निभा यस्याः सा चन्द्रनिभा
samasa.vigraha_iast: candrasya nibhā iva nibhā yasyāḥ sā candranibhā
samasa.explanation: nibhā 'luster, appearance' (at the end of a compound, 'resembling'): 'She whose luster is like the moon's'. Read with nibha as an adjective, 'like the moon', the sense is the same.

components.meaning: luster, appearance; at the end of a compound 'resembling'

names.meaning: She who is resplendent like the moon
names.significance: Meditated on in the head (name 591), She is cool and white like the full moon, the nectar-giving light at the crown.

samasa.vigraha: भाले तिष्ठति इति भालस्था
samasa.vigraha_iast: bhāle tiṣṭhati iti bhālasthā
samasa.explanation: -stha 'standing, abiding' is formed from √sthā with the suffix ka when a noun precedes (Pāṇini 3.2.4 supi sthaḥ), and takes the feminine -ā; bhāla 'forehead' is its locative complement: 'She who abides in the forehead'.

names.meaning: She who resides in the forehead (between the eyebrows)
names.significance: At the brow, the place of the ājñā center, She is meditated on as shining with the colors of the rainbow (name 594).

sandhi.rule: final s becomes visarga before a hard consonant (Pāṇini 8.2.66 with 8.3.15 kharavasānayor visarjanīyaḥ)

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi of resemblance (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: इन्द्रस्य धनुः इन्द्रधनुः; इन्द्रधनुषः प्रभा इव प्रभा यस्याः सा इन्द्रधनुःप्रभा
samasa.vigraha_iast: indrasya dhanuḥ indradhanuḥ; indradhanuṣaḥ prabhā iva prabhā yasyāḥ sā indradhanuḥprabhā
samasa.explanation: (1) indra-dhanus 'Indra's bow', the rainbow (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) A bahuvrīhi of resemblance: 'She whose radiance is like the radiance of the rainbow'.

components.note: s-stem; indradhanus 'Indra's bow' is the rainbow

names.meaning: She who is resplendent like the rainbow
names.significance: The rainbow holds every color at once: so, at the brow (name 593), She is seen in many hues.

samasa.vigraha: हृदये तिष्ठति इति हृदयस्था
samasa.vigraha_iast: hṛdaye tiṣṭhati iti hṛdayasthā
samasa.explanation: As in name 593: -stha from √sthā with ka (Pāṇini 3.2.4), feminine -ā, with hṛdaya 'heart' as its locative complement.

names.meaning: She who resides in the heart
names.significance: In the heart, the seat of the Self, She is meditated on as shining like the sun (name 596).

samasa.vigraha: रवेः प्रख्या इव प्रख्या यस्याः सा रविप्रख्या
samasa.vigraha_iast: raveḥ prakhyā iva prakhyā yasyāḥ sā raviprakhyā
samasa.explanation: prakhyā 'brightness, appearance' (at the end of a compound, 'like'): 'She whose brightness is like the sun's'.

components.meaning: brightness, appearance; at the end of a compound 'resembling'

names.meaning: She who shines like the sun
names.significance: In the heart (name 595) She is the inner sun that lights all experience.

meaning_check.note: 'special brilliance' is not in the name; prakhyā is 'brightness, likeness'.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: saptamī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa and bahuvrīhi)
samasa.vigraha: त्रयः कोणाः यस्य तत् त्रिकोणम्; त्रिकोणस्य अन्तरम् त्रिकोणान्तरम्; त्रिकोणान्तरे दीपिका त्रिकोणान्तरदीपिका
samasa.vigraha_iast: trayaḥ koṇāḥ yasya tat trikoṇam; trikoṇasya antaram trikoṇāntaram; trikoṇāntare dīpikā trikoṇāntaradīpikā
samasa.explanation: (1) tri-koṇa 'that which has three angles', the triangle (bahuvrīhi). (2) trikoṇa-antara 'the inside of the triangle' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) dīpikā 'lamp' is the head and the interior is its place, in the locative: 'the lamp within the triangle'.

names.meaning: She who shines as a light within the triangle
names.significance: The triangle is traditionally both the one in the mūlādhāra where kuṇḍalinī rests and the innermost triangle of the Śrīcakra around the bindu; there She burns as a steady flame.

components.note: dakṣa + the patronymic suffix -āyana (dākṣāyaṇa, n → ṇ after ṣ), feminine -ī

names.meaning: She who is Satī, the daughter of Dakṣa Prajāpati
names.significance: As Satī She was born to Dakṣa and gave up that body when he insulted Śiva at his sacrifice (name 600), to be born again as Pārvatī.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'satIdevI', 'dakSha prajApati' put into IAST.

samasa.vigraha: दैत्यानाम् हन्त्री दैत्यहन्त्री
samasa.vigraha_iast: daityānām hantrī daityahantrī
samasa.explanation: hantrī 'slayer' (agent noun) is the head and the daityas are its object in the genitive.

components.meaning: daitya, a son of Diti; a demon opposed to the gods

names.meaning: She who is the killer of demons
names.significance: As Durgā and Caṇḍikā, and as Lalitā against Bhaṇḍa, She destroys the powers hostile to the gods; inwardly, the demonic tendencies of the mind.

samasa.vigraha: दक्षस्य यज्ञः दक्षयज्ञः; दक्षयज्ञस्य विनाशिनी दक्षयज्ञविनाशिनी
samasa.vigraha_iast: dakṣasya yajñaḥ dakṣayajñaḥ; dakṣayajñasya vināśinī dakṣayajñavināśinī
samasa.explanation: (1) dakṣa-yajña 'Dakṣa's sacrifice' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) vināśinī 'destroyer' is the head and takes the sacrifice in the genitive.

components.note: vi + causative of √naś, agent suffix -in, feminine -ī

names.meaning: She who is the destroyer of Dakṣa's sacrifice
names.significance: After Satī gave up her body at Dakṣa's sacrifice, Śiva's wrath, in the form of Vīrabhadra with Bhadrakālī, laid it waste; traditionally the episode warns against ritual performed without devotion to the Lord.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'dakSha' put into IAST; wording tightened.

verse_notes.note: Name 545: divide pulomajā + arcitā (Śacī + 'worshipped'). Name 547 reads bandhurālakā here; the old name list had barbarālakā (see the name's variants).
Name 550 is one compound, viyad-ādi-jagat-prasūḥ, though it was once printed as two words; the d is the voiced t of viyat 'ether'.

external_sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101); the avagraha (ऽ) marks the absorbed initial a of acintya

verse_notes.note: Divide agragaṇyā + acintyarūpā: the avagraha shows that the next name begins with the negative a- ('inconceivable'), not cintya ('conceivable').
Names 559–561 return briefly to Her physical beauty (betel-filled mouth, pomegranate-red complexion, doe's eyes) amid names of Her power.

external_sandhi.rule: visarga becomes r before a voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ)

verse_notes.note: Name 570 refers to the four attitudes of Yoga Sūtra 1.33 (friendliness, compassion, gladness, equanimity).
Names 572 and 573 are each written as two words, parā śaktiḥ and parā niṣṭhā: adjective and noun in agreement, each pair counted as one name. Name 575: divide pāna + alasā ('languid from drinking').

external_sandhi.rule: visarga becomes r before a voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ)

verse_notes.note: Name 579: dorlatā is dos 'arm' + latā 'creeper'; the r is the s of dos before l.
Names 583–589 are names of the mantra: the Vidyās, the sixteen-syllable Ṣoḍaśī, the three kūṭas of the Pañcadaśī.

external_sandhi.rule: guṇa: ā + i → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

verse_notes.note: Divide bhālasthā + indradhanuḥprabhā. Names 591–597 (into śloka 120) place Her at four points for meditation: in the head like the moon, at the brow like the rainbow, in the heart like the sun, in the triangle as a lamp.
Names 598 and 600 recall the Dakṣa episode: Satī, Dakṣa's daughter, and the destruction of his sacrifice.

report.summary: Checked all 59 names of ślokas 111–120 against text.json: sandhi at every member junction and visible prefix junction, a layered samāsa with pausa-form vigrahas, and each meaning against that analysis. Name 552's old meaning was truncated (death was missing) and was replaced; 36 others were tidied (ITRANS to IAST, words not in the name removed, e.g. 'and sorrows' in 551, 'three worlds' in 582), and 575's inner reading was moved to the significance. Names 572–573 are read as adjective-noun phrases (parā śaktiḥ, parā niṣṭhā), not compounds, since the feminine parā is kept; 590's kiṅkarībhūta is a cvi formation. No problem was found in the Sanskrit; the reading of 547 (bandhurālakā, with barbarālakā as a variant) is flagged for review, and external sandhi joins names in ślokas 113, 115, 117 and 119.
